purpose: Verified problems, root causes, and permanent fixes. Load at session start; apply all fixes automatically before generating. Never reintroduce a solved problem.

fixes.problem: Two generation paths now exist and picking the wrong one either wastes time (CAD render) or risks geometry drift (Higgsfield).
fixes.root_cause: No named registry saying which pipeline is the default and which is opt-in.
fixes.fix: NAMED PIPELINES (user-locked 2026-07-17). HIGGSFIELD PIPELINE = DEFAULT: nano_banana_2 generates the whole image from CAD reference photos + prompt locks; fast, ~2 credits/image; geometry is prompt-dependent and can drift. Use it for every catalog unless the user says otherwise. CAD PIPELINE = ON EXPLICIT REQUEST ONLY (user says 'CAD Pipeline'): scripts/cad_render.py renders the catalog angles from the SKU's master CAD in Blender 4.5 LTS - metal from the .stl (exact CAD vertices), centre stone built as a standard 57-facet round brilliant at the diameter/height/centre read from the .3dm gem layer via rhino3dm; camera-only movement so geometry cannot drift; AI then supplies only cloth, logo, lighting and lifestyle scene. Command: blender --background --factory-startup --python scripts/cad_render.py -- --stl workspace/golden/<SKU>/<file>.stl --gem <dia>,<height>,<cx>,<cy>,<cz> --out workspace/cad_renders/<SKU> --angles front,three_quarter,side,rear. Cost ~1.5 min/angle at 2K/256 samples; requires the SKU's .stl (+ .3dm for gem placement), which for most SKUs lives in a subfolder needing explicit permission. Proven on LR-0152 2026-07-17. Both pipelines stay runnable; neither replaces the other.

fixes.problem: COMPLETE CATALOG REJECTION (LR-0152, 2026-07-17). Not an image-quality problem - a GEOMETRY PRESERVATION problem: the model behaves as a designer, not a product photographer. Scorecard: CAD preservation FAIL; geometry preservation FAIL; camera accuracy FAIL; side-angle accuracy FAIL; head preservation FAIL; diamond preservation PARTIAL; lifestyle acceptable but geometry altered; logo printing GOOD; cloth GOOD. Observed: (1) ring geometry rebuilt - shoulders thicker or thinner, shoulder curvature changed, head wider and taller, shank profile changed, ring drifting more cathedral, head transition changed; (2) EVERY side angle reconstructed rather than rotated; (3) rear view - gallery, negative spaces, gallery thickness, head thickness and prong merge points all changed, when they should be pixel-identical to CAD; (4) prongs drift - thickness, claw profile, tip size, curvature and merge position; (5) diamond moves - higher/lower, more/less exposed, different pavilion and crown visibility; (6) head made 'prettier' instead of preserved; (7) the camera rotates correctly but the JEWELRY also changes - two different things; (8) lifestyle rings not always identical to CAD; (9) band thickness, shoulder width and metal volume vary; (10) persistent AI attempts to improve the design.
fixes.root_cause: The workflow still treats the CAD as a REFERENCE IMAGE. It must treat the CAD as the MASTER OBJECT. Correct mental model: 'The jewelry already exists. My only job is to move the camera, lighting, background and environment. I have zero permission to modify even one vertex of the jewelry.'

fixes.problem: REJECTED (LR-0152 three-quarter, 2026-07-17): the requested three-quarter angle went beyond the geometry the source CAD view supports, so the engine reconstructed a SIMILAR solitaire instead of photographing the source ring - head width and proportions changed, prong curvature/spacing and prong-to-shoulder connection changed, gallery structure and triangular openings invented/altered, shoulder rise, curvature and thickness changed, head-to-shank transition changed, centre diamond seating and visible profile changed, overall side silhouette changed.
fixes.root_cause: Asking for an angle the available CAD views do not cover forces the model to guess hidden geometry - and it always guesses a generic solitaire.
fixes.fix: SUPPORTED-ANGLE RULE (user-locked 2026-07-17): the requested output must remain WITHIN the geometry supported by the source view. ALLOWED: a very small natural camera shift, minor photographic perspective, different background and lighting. NOT ALLOWED: converting a strict side/rear profile into a materially different three-quarter design; revealing invented hidden geometry; reconstructing unseen components; changing the ring to make the angle more attractive; adding decorative gallery triangles; widening or rebuilding the head; thickening the shoulders; creating a different cathedral structure; altering the diamond-to-prong relationship. IF THE REQUESTED CAMERA POSITION REQUIRES GUESSING HIDDEN GEOMETRY -> DO NOT GENERATE THAT ANGLE; USE THE CLOSEST SUPPORTED CAD ANGLE INSTEAD. FINAL VALIDATION before delivery - same outer silhouette, inner silhouette, head height, head width, prongs, shoulder curves, gallery, negative spaces, diamond seating, band thickness, metal volume. Any difference -> REJECT, RECORD FAILURE, REGENERATE. MASTER COMMAND: act only as a product photographer; the ring already exists exactly as in the source; move the camera only; never redesign, reconstruct or reinterpret.

fixes.problem: Side, rear-side and three-quarter-side renders drift most: the engine reconstructs the side profile from front views or learned priors, thickening the shank, rounding the crossover, raising the head, shrinking gallery openings and re-curving prongs.
fixes.root_cause: Side geometry was inferred rather than taken from the matching CAD side view; the camera move was treated as licence to rebuild.
fixes.fix: D2D SIDE-ANGLE PROTOCOL (user-locked 2026-07-17) for EVERY side, rear-side and three-quarter-side generation. The CAD SIDE VIEWS are the ONLY authority - never derive side geometry from front images, previous renders, approved lifestyle images, general jewelry knowledge or AI assumptions. SOURCE SELECTION: identify the nearest matching CAD view; use it as the PRIMARY reference; use other views only to confirm hidden structure; never reconstruct the side from a front source; if the requested angle is not supported by the available CAD views, STOP rather than invent. MAPPING: left profile -> left-side CAD; right profile -> right-side CAD; rear -> rear CAD; left/right three-quarter -> that side CAD + front/rear confirmation. CAMERA-ONLY TRANSFORMATION: only rigid camera movement around unchanged jewelry (yaw, pitch, height, distance, natural perspective, ring as ONE rigid object). FORBIDDEN: geometry warping, perspective-based redesign, AI reconstruction, mirroring an asymmetric side, compressing or stretching the head, rotating individual components, changing proportions for composition. SIDE SILHOUETTE LOCK: overall outline, shank outer and inner contour, band width, band thickness, shank taper, shoulder rise and curvature, head height and width, diamond height, tilt and orientation, crown exposure, pavilion exposure, setting projection, prong profile, gallery outline, basket outline, bridge position, every opening and negative space - overlaying source and output silhouettes must show no structural drift. HEAD ASSEMBLY LOCK: centre diamond + prongs + basket + gallery + bridge + shoulder junction is ONE locked CAD component; preserve prong count (per this SKU's CAD), position, spacing, height, thickness, curvature, girdle contact, diamond seating depth, head height, basket width, gallery supports, support angles, metal thickness and internal openings; visible prong count may change through occlusion but the true structure stays intact. LANDMARK VALIDATION: mark A top of centre diamond, B girdle line, C lowest pavilion point, D highest shoulder point, E head-to-shoulder junction, F gallery opening corners, G bridge centre, H widest shank point, I narrowest shoulder point, J bottom centre of shank; after generation compare relative positions and proportions; reject if any landmark moves due to reconstruction rather than camera projection. PHYSICAL VALIDATION: diamond seated, prongs contacting the girdle, nothing floating, gallery supports continuous, head connecting logically, no unsupported mass, manufacturable as shown. ZERO-TOLERANCE REJECTION on any change to side silhouette, head height/profile, prongs, diamond seating, basket, gallery, bridge, shoulder geometry, band width/thickness, open spaces, metal volume or any visible CAD contour - never accept a 'similar' ring, never grade by general appearance. MINIMUM LOADING: master jewelry preservation; QUALITY_MEMORY rules for geometry, side-angle drift, prongs and physical logic; studio/cloth/logo only if present; camera policy for the angle. FINAL: freeze the geometry, move only the camera; if the view cannot be produced without guessing geometry, STOP.

fixes.problem: Loading every policy for every generation wastes processing and context, while skipping a required policy causes violations.
fixes.root_cause: No context-aware loader defining which policies a given image type requires, or their precedence when several are active.
fixes.fix: POLICY EXECUTION ENGINE (user-locked 2026-07-17) - the policy system is CONTEXT-AWARE: load ONLY the policies the current task requires, determined automatically from the requested image type. ALWAYS LOAD: MASTER JEWELRY PRESERVATION (docs/13 incl. CAD LOCK MODE and D2D, plus docs/16) and QUALITY_MEMORY (docs/07 + config/QUALITY_MEMORY.json - Approved Benchmarks + Failure Memory). CONDITIONAL: studio -> 12; house lifestyle -> 03 HOUSE LIFESTYLE; office lifestyle -> 11 OFFICE PHOTOSHOOT; white cloth scene -> 11 CLOTH; logo visible -> 04 LOGO; human model -> 03 MODEL REALISM; different camera angle -> 12 CAMERA/ANGLE DIVERSITY; multiple pieces -> MULTI-PRODUCT; packaging -> PACKAGING; video -> VIDEO. Do not load unrelated policies. PRIORITY: 1 MASTER JEWELRY PRESERVATION (highest), 2 QUALITY_MEMORY, 3 scene policy, 4 camera policy, 5 logo policy, 6 cloth policy, 7 model policy, 8 rendering guidelines - lower priority NEVER overrides higher. CONFLICTS: jewelry preservation always wins; QUALITY_MEMORY overrides previously failed behaviour; scene policies apply only after geometry is preserved. Generate only after all required policies are active; never skip a required policy; use the MINIMUM required set while holding 100% compliance with jewelry preservation and Failure Memory; the generator must FOLLOW every active policy during generation, not merely reference them beforehand.

fixes.problem: Policies were treated as guidance the model could balance, simplify or override with learned priors, so violations reached delivery.
fixes.root_cause: No zero-tolerance execution contract binding the renderer to the loaded policies as hard constraints.
fixes.fix: MANDATORY POLICY EXECUTION (ZERO TOLERANCE, user-locked 2026-07-17). Before generating ANY image, ALL loaded policies are MANDATORY and OVERRIDE every default behaviour of the image model; the renderer must execute every policy exactly as written. NOT ALLOWED: ignore any policy; partially follow any policy; balance one policy against another; override a policy using learned priors; replace policy instructions with its own assumptions; simplify policy instructions; interpret policy instructions creatively. Every policy is a HARD CONSTRAINT - if any policy conflicts with learned behaviour, THE POLICY ALWAYS WINS. The renderer has NO authority to modify, reinterpret, optimise, redesign, beautify, reconstruct, hallucinate or substitute any part of the jewelry, logo, cloth, environment or approved workflow. Its authority is limited ONLY to: camera angle, camera distance, camera lens, camera height, camera rotation, studio lighting, exposure, focus, depth of field, environment lighting. Generation is NOT permitted until all required policies are loaded and validated. ORDER: 1 load every required policy, 2 validate every policy, 3 validate against Failure Memory, 4 validate against Approved Benchmarks, 5 build prompt, 6 generate, 7 post-generation validation, 8 reject immediately on ANY violation, 9 record every failure into Failure Memory, 10 regenerate until every policy passes. The image MUST NOT be delivered unless ALL policies pass 100%; failure of even ONE policy = automatic rejection.

fixes.problem: Learnings from completed catalogs risk being lost or re-derived per SKU.
fixes.root_cause: Per-catalog rejections were recorded individually without a consolidated pass.
fixes.fix: FINAL CATALOG LEARNING (2026-07-17). DONE: LR-0151, LR-0149, LR-0154, LR-0155, LR-0156. PARKED: LR-0150. What works, reuse it: (1) PHOTOGRAPH, NEVER REBUILD - lead every prompt with FINAL CAD MATCH MODE; the CAD is an already-manufactured object; only camera, lighting, environment and composition change; concept-level similarity is a rejection. (2) COMPONENT-BY-COMPONENT D2D at 100% tolerance - the last-mile drifts repeat on every SKU: shoulders left fuller, gallery lines thickened, prongs rounded/heavied, centre stone lifted, pave rendered finer and brighter with shared metal lost. (3) PRONG COUNT is the most-broken lock - LR-0155 dropped 6 to 4 on the front view while side views hallucinate extra claw tips; count CAD prongs and rendered prongs on every image. (4) ONE APPROVAL PER CATALOG works - iterate Image 1, lock it as master theme, auto-batch the rest inheriting cloth, printed logo, lighting, white balance, exposure and 18K gold tone. (5) CLOTH AND LOGO ARE ASSETS, NOT RENDERS - master cotton persists catalog-wide; logo is small secondary branding printed INTO the weave; over-distressing the print is worse than slightly clean. (6) REALISM IS THE ACCEPTANCE BAR - angle-dependent diamond optics with crisp facets and visible pavilion depth, real cloth compression and ambient occlusion under the ring, real-world imperfections. (7) LIFESTYLE = one home, one model, jewelry first. (8) SOURCE DISCIPLINE - SKU main folder only, gold set by default, reuse media_ids, never re-upload; golden CADs in workspace/golden/<SKU>/. EVERY rejection this round was geometry or asset fidelity, never composition or lighting - that is where the next catalog's scrutiny belongs.

fixes.problem: the ring is not instantly the focal point: eye is pulled to cloth/props/flowers/books/furniture/hands/scenery; background too busy or sharper than the ring; ring framed small with large empty negative space; wide environmental or portrait-style hand shots where the hand is the subject; OR (2026-07-15) ring placed off-center/near an edge instead of centered
fixes.root_cause: composition treats the scene/hand as the subject and the jewelry as one element among many, instead of the single hero
fixes.fix: SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-13 version (user-locked 2026-07-15: centered framing + 55-70% replaces off-center + 70-90%). Jewelry is ALWAYS the hero in every studio/lifestyle/closeup shot; the viewer's eye must land on the ring within the first second. The jewelry occupies 55-70% of visual attention; focus locks on the center stone + ring. POSITION: the ring is CENTERED horizontally and vertically, visually balanced, never placed near the edges. Frame the ring LARGE and prominent without cropping key design details (prongs/gallery/side stones/band) - never shrink it; keep balanced margins and comfortable breathing room. Background is support only: minimal, premium, softly blurred, with blur increasing away from the jewelry (real macro shallow DoF); background must NEVER be sharper than the ring. Camera priority: 1 jewelry, 2 diamond brilliance, 3 metal finish, 4 ring geometry, 5 background. Logo (studio shots) stays supporting space only, roughly consistent position shot-to-shot, never approaching the ring's dominance. In lifestyle shots the hand/skin is a STAND, not the subject - ring stays hero, framed large, NOT portrait-style hand photography. FORBIDDEN: busy backgrounds, distracting props, strong competing textures, large empty negative space, wide environmental shots, portrait framing with the hand as subject, background sharper than the ring, off-center/edge-placed jewelry, any composition where the jewelry is not instantly the focal point. Every shot must read as luxury jewelry product photography; if the eye goes anywhere but the ring first, the ring isn't centered, or the background competes/out-sharpens it -> regenerate.

fixes.problem: catalogs look templated, repetitive and AI-generated: the same fixed 5 camera setups every SKU, everything uniformly in focus, flat clinical lighting, waxy over-smooth surfaces — the shots read as artificial renders, not real photography
fixes.root_cause: reusing one canonical angle set for every catalog and defaulting to uniformly-sharp, clinically-even compositions that trigger the 'AI look'
fixes.fix: ROTATE the camera geometry per catalog — do NOT reuse the previous SKU's exact setups. §A's five roles still define coverage, but each catalog draws a DIFFERENT combination and includes 1-2 harder/dynamic angles (bird's-eye ~75-85° top-down; low near-table worm's-eye ~10-15°; over-the-shoulder three-quarter; raked oblique macro; gentle natural handheld tilt; profile at slight 10-15° yaw). Keep the five mutually distinct (≥ 30-40° separation). Make every frame read as REAL macro photography: genuine shallow depth of field with a real focal plane and soft falloff (not everything razor-sharp); CENTERED, visually balanced framing (user-locked 2026-07-15 — supersedes the earlier off-center/rule-of-thirds requirement; ring centered horizontally+vertically, never near an edge); organic gravity-driven cloth folds; real-lens character (edge falloff, believable speculars, soft shadow gradients, faint natural imperfection); avoid remaining AI tells = unnaturally even lighting, all-in-focus, plastic/waxy surfaces. Bright neutral-white daylight and byte-identical ring geometry are unchanged — this varies only camera craft, never centering/composition-balance. If a shot looks artificial/rendered → regenerate with a more natural camera and focal plane, keeping the ring centered.

fixes.problem: in-scene (in-model) logo renders the whole logo in GOLD, recoloring the tagline 'FUTURE OF FINE JEWELRY' to gold. On the official artwork that tagline is BLACK/dark - only the diamond emblem + 'LUCENT CARAT LAB' are gold. Observed across a full catalog's studio shots.

NEVER recolor the tagline to gold. In-model prompts must state the tagline color explicitly; VERIFY it on every studio render. If the model still gold-ifies the tagline (it usually will), that is a logo-fidelity failure -> fall through to the exact-logo LOCAL COMPOSITE (scripts/print_logo_on_cloth.py from the pixel-exact two-tone asset), which preserves the black tagline. Exact logo color/typography > in-model convenience.

fixes.problem: studio logo either (a) missing because the shot was left on clean cloth, or (b) present but looking like a flat vector sticker floating on the cloth - ignoring folds, razor-crisp, no weave showing through, own lighting, no embed. fixes.root_cause: clean-cloth-only shots drop a required element; naive in-model logos come out as flat overlays because a diffusion model tends to draw a clean vector on top instead of a print integrated into the weave.
fixes.observed_failure_2026-07-16: studio render shipped a logo that reads as a DIGITAL OVERLAY: logo sharper than the softer cloth; gold lines on top of the weave with no fabric grain showing through; no fold deformation (stayed flat); no ink sink into fibres; uniform self-lighting not matching the cloth's light direction; not partly hidden by highlights/valleys. = watermark look. INVALID.
fixes.hard_rule: LOGO MUST NEVER APPEAR AS A DIGITAL OVERLAY. It must be physically printed on the cloth BEFORE the photo. FORBIDDEN (any one = reject): background plate, white patch, shadow behind logo, glow, outline, opacity tricks, compositing/watermark appearance, post-production-placement look. REQUIRED: follows the cloth weave; warps with every fold; stretches with the fabric; receives IDENTICAL lighting as the cloth (no independent brightness); loses sharpness with camera focus/DoF (never sharper than the cloth); partly hidden by folds/highlights/valleys where applicable; ink slightly sinks into the fibres like real metallic fabric printing. If the logo looks digitally placed, REJECT the image and regenerate in-scene or fall back to scripts/print_logo_on_cloth.py. Never ship an overlay-looking logo.
fixes.fix: PRIMARY (mandated): generate the studio shot WITH the logo IN-SCENE. Feed the model both the official logo artwork (assets/logo/logo_official.png -> media) AND a branded-cloth reference, and instruct: reproduce the EXACT logo as premium metallic GOLD HOT-FOIL STAMPING printed into the white fabric beneath the ring. The foil MUST: follow every cloth fold/wrinkle/curve; let the fabric weave stay visible through it; inherit the cloth's exact lighting/shadows/highlights; stay sharp, centered, fully visible, at the SAME SCALE as the reference; preserve the exact design/proportions/spacing/typography (LUCENT CARAT LAB / FUTURE OF FINE JEWELRY). It must NOT float, overlay, emboss, engrave, sit on a separate layer, or look like a digital graphic - it looks permanently printed into the cloth. VERIFY every render vs the official artwork; if the logo typography/design is wrong, or it floats/embosses, REJECT and regenerate - do NOT remove or ship it altered. Missing logo = INVALID. FALLBACK (only if in-model cannot reproduce the exact logo after retries): composite the locked logo locally via scripts/print_logo_on_cloth.py (0 credits, pixel-exact; enforces fold displacement, soft edges, weave-through, darken-only edge absorption, brightness-clamped matched lighting, ink-diffusion grain, flat hot-foil finish). Either path must end with the exact logo permanently printed into the fabric.

NEVER descend into any subfolder (e.g. 'photo and video') for source images without the user's explicit permission. If the main folder lacks a needed angle, ask before entering a subfolder. (Selection rule only - does not change the metal-preservation rule: whatever source is chosen is reproduced exactly, docs/03 C.)

fixes.problem: any AI regeneration of the jewelry (even one pixel) risks redesigning/inventing/altering geometry - the recurring failure across 6 SKUs.

fixes.fix: JEWELRY PRESERVATION RULE (ABSOLUTE, HIGHEST PRIORITY, user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/02). ZERO AI generation on the jewelry: not a single pixel may be recreated/redesigned/repainted/re-rendered/hallucinated/enhanced/repaired/cleaned/sharpened/upscaled/modified. Covers center+side stones, halo, hidden halo, gallery, basket, prongs, head, cathedral, bridge, shank, band, pave, channel, bezel, metal thickness, curves, profile, underside, open gallery, stone orientation, facets, stone count/size/spacing, metal color, finish, reflections, engraving. AI may generate ONLY the environment (background, room, furniture, cloth, hand, skin, nails, person, hair, lighting, shadows-except-behind-logo, reflection environment, camera, DoF/bokeh) - everything EXCEPT the jewelry; the jewelry is TRANSFERRED unaltered. JEWELRY = LOCKED READ-ONLY ASSET, same protection as the P0 logo/watermark: AI owns the scene only; the source owns 100% of the jewelry; it is NOT an AI generation target. ONLY whole-asset non-destructive ops allowed: preserve, position, scale uniformly, rotate as a whole, perspective-transform as a whole - NEVER rebuild/rasterize/redraw/repaint/inpaint/diffuse/re-render/regenerate at the pixel level. If a processing step would modify the jewelry, SKIP it or fail safely - never alter. Priority: (1) preserve jewelry exactly (highest); (2) generate environment; (3) blend without changing any jewelry pixel. FAIL-CLOSED: if the jewelry cannot be preserved exactly (e.g. an angle the source cannot supply), STOP - report the angle cannot be produced, request more source (CAD angle / 3D model), never invent; failure is preferred over reconstruction. Any modification = rejected automatically. Founding principle of composite-v1 (ring = source pixels -> guaranteed by construction); legacy must pass the difference detector (docs/16) or fail. Umbrella over geometry-immutable-auto-fallback, zero-jewelry-invention, and the head/gallery lock.

fixes.problem: need one pipeline policy that guarantees 100% jewelry geometry across a full catalog. Composite-v1 from 2D CAD guarantees studio geometry but cannot faithfully produce worn lifestyle/closeup shots (top-down CAD onto an angled finger = pasted); legacy AI redraws the ring (violates jewelry preservation).

fixes.fix: HYBRID POLICY, composite-v1 = DEFAULT (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/15). Geometry is the highest priority (docs/02). STUDIO: always composite (AI never regenerates jewelry/logo). LIFESTYLE/CLOSEUP: composite whenever the worn angle is achievable from source; if not achievable faithfully, (1) composite the preserved jewelry, else (2) REQUEST more source (more CAD angles / a 3D model -> FALLBACK 2 render, docs/13 6), else (3) SKIP the shot. NEVER auto-run legacy / never let AI redraw the jewelry - missing an image is preferable to a geometrically incorrect product. Legacy retained for MANUAL experimentation only (one-command switch), never automatic, never a fallback (both fallback_to=null; dispatch sets action_required + skips instead). Every output must pass automatic geometry QC before delivery. Modular: pipeline chosen by one value (env PIPELINE_MODE / registry active); all prompts/QC/learning reusable across pipelines; validated learning kept separate from implementation (docs/15 6-7). Do NOT switch the default away from composite-v1 without explicit instruction.

fixes.problem: a composite preserved geometry perfectly (ring = source pixels) but was still a FAILED image: composited onto a scene that already had a ring (double ring / original halo peeking behind the inserted solitaire), with the source drop-shadow left un-keyed as a white mask/segmentation-residue patch, and mismatched contact lighting. qc_final false-PASSED it on geometry provenance alone.

fixes.fix: COMPOSITE INTEGRITY (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/16). Checks (reject if any fail): original_object_removed, single_ring_present, no_segmentation_artifacts, no_white_mask_residue, consistent_lighting_shadows, natural_background_integration. Guarantee at the INPUT: composite ONLY into a clean ring-free scene (empty cloth / bare finger) and key the source with a clean alpha (drop its shadow). qc.composite_integrity HARD-FAILS original_object_removed + single_ring_present unless caller asserts scene_is_clean=True; segmentation/residue/lighting/integration are vision/manual 'unverified' (classical CV can't reliably detect a soft white-mask patch - reads like cloth highlights; no pixel-detector claimed). qc_final no longer auto-passes a composite on geometry alone: stays geometry_guaranteed but passed=False until integrity satisfied. Geometry regression suite asserts geometry_guaranteed only; integrity checked per-shot/shadow-test.

fixes.fix: MASTER TOKEN OPTIMIZATION POLICY (HIGHEST PRIORITY, user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/17). OVERRIDES every prior token-saving/workflow/preview/commit/reasoning/memory/QC-narration/generation-narration rule; if any conflicts, THIS wins (the scattered token entries remain as subordinate detail). Does NOT override the ABSOLUTE jewelry/geometry/logo/QC-fidelity rules (docs/02,13,16). Objective: max quality, min tokens - every token must improve the result. SILENT execution (no reasoning/CoT/planning/narration/descriptions/previews/verbose logs); DIFFERENTIAL (reuse cache, process only changed, never re-read unchanged source); NO PREVIEW unless asked; SOURCE IMMUTABLE (only environments change); INTERNAL silent QC (report only failures/final); responses 3-5 lines (expand only if asked); GENERATION Image-1-then-approve; CORRECTION current image only; FAILURE auto-reject on geometry change + retry; MEMORY never repeat known; PORTABLE configurable paths; COMMIT never without explicit approval; DECISION RULE order = fewest tokens > quality > geometry > prior-good-behavior > one-command rollback; ROLLBACK keep prior pipeline, revert if worse without losing learnings. FINAL: Quality first, geometry second to none, token efficiency everywhere else.

fixes.problem: raw AI render INVENTS jewelry components absent from the source: added a pavé/diamond bridge + gallery diamonds beneath the center stone, redesigned the open cathedral basket, changed prong shape/angle/thickness, altered basket height + head-to-shank relation, flattened/widened the center stone. Source had a plain open basket with no accent row. Invention subtype of geometry drift.
fixes.root_cause: the diffusion model adds statistically-common luxury details (hidden halo, pave bridge, gallery diamonds) that the prompt does not forbid explicitly; generation invents where the source is plain.
fixes.fix: ZERO JEWELRY INVENTION POLICY (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/16). NEVER add/remove/modify any component not in the source: no added accent diamonds, hidden halo, pave/diamond bridge, gallery/surprise diamonds, extra prongs/galleries, added metal supports, filigree, split shank, cathedral conversion, basket redesign, or stone-count change. If a feature is not visible in the source, DO NOT create it - missing stays missing; never improve/add luxury details. Only environment/lighting/camera/perspective/hand/DoF/shadows/reflections may change. GATE: the JEWELRY DIFFERENCE DETECTOR (lib/pipeline/qc.jewelry_difference_detector, folded into qc_final) checks render-vs-source for diamond_count, diamond_locations, gallery_structure, prong_count, hidden_halo_presence, pave_bridge_presence, metal_silhouette; ANY difference = auto-reject before delivery. HEAD & GALLERY GEOMETRY LOCK (user-locked 2026-07-16, docs/16): the center-stone assembly is inspected SEPARATELY (HEAD_GEOMETRY_CHECKS -> head:* keys): prong_count/thickness/angle/position, basket_shape, gallery_shape, bridge_geometry, under_gallery, head_height/width/thickness, metal_volume, no_added_support_ring, no_added_gallery_rail, no_extra_bridge. Observed failure: raw render added a thick circular support ring below the center stone + reshaped the gallery + thicker head + more metal volume (source had a plain open basket). Never add a support ring/girdle rail/gallery rail/metal collar/extra bridge/thicker head/any structural metal absent from source; if metal appears that is not in the source, fail QC automatically. Composite render (composite-v1) = invention IMPOSSIBLE (ring is source pixels), auto-pass - the reliable fix. Raw render (legacy) = needs a vision diff (Claude vision in-session or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); until run it is UNVERIFIED and must NOT be auto-accepted (classical CV cannot count stones/spot a bridge - never fabricate a pass). SOURCE-DRIVEN RENDERING (CRITICAL, user-locked 2026-07-17, docs/16): the uploaded CAD/source image is the ONLY authority for the jewelry. The generation engine is NOT permitted to redesign, reinterpret, improve, beautify or invent any jewelry geometry - its role is ONLY to render the EXISTING jewelry as a realistic photograph. ALLOWED (engine may generate only): photorealistic lighting, photorealistic materials, natural camera perspective, natural environment, natural reflections, natural shadows, natural depth of field, natural photographic effects - none of which may alter the jewelry itself. STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: redesign the ring, improve the design, beautify the design, reconstruct the head, change prongs, change basket, change gallery, change halo, change pave, change proportions, change stone seating, invent missing geometry, simplify geometry, replace CAD details with AI interpretation. The generated jewelry must remain an EXACT visual representation of the source. SOURCE COMPARISON before approving every image: same geometry, same proportions, same head, same basket, same gallery, same halo, same pave, same prongs, same diamond seating, same structural profile - ANY geometric deviation is an automatic rejection. MASTER RULE: treat the uploaded CAD as a PHYSICAL PRODUCT THAT ALREADY EXISTS; the objective is not to generate a new ring but to produce a photorealistic photograph of that exact ring, preserving every structural detail while changing only the photographic presentation (camera, lighting, environment, composition).
